A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, and core results. The main text and Appendices A-H are readable, and figures, tables, and proofs can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original multiset and graph separation experiments and evaluations of SortMPNN and AdaptMPNN on TUDatasets, LRGB, and ZINC12K, documented in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds trained multiset classification results in Figure 7 and a smaller-tree separation experiment in Appendix G.4.

M1.justification: The multiset embeddings, SortMPNN and AdaptMPNN procedures, and architectural variants in Appendix G.2 are unchanged. The new theoretical analysis and experiments evaluate existing methods.

E1.justification: Appendix G.3 adds supervised classification of multisets with 1, 3, 7, or 15 equal moments, including a distinct adversarial condition with added elements +2 and -2. This extends the existing synthetic coverage; the real-world graph datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2-5 retain their corresponding comparator sets, including GIN, GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GINE, and GatedGCN. Figure 7 uses the existing sorting, adaptive ReLU, ReLU, and smooth embeddings rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: The new multiset classification experiments specify 100 pairs per dataset, scaling values from 0.01 to 0.1, and an 80/10/10 training/validation/test split. Appendix G.4 additionally reports training on height-3 trees with one message-passing layer. These are added protocols; existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds controlled analyses linking equal-moment difficulty to trained classification accuracy and testing whether extreme elements defeat adaptive ReLU. Appendix G.4 adds a reduced-depth experiment probing whether ReLU and smooth MPNNs differ on smaller adversarial trees.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean/standard-deviation reporting, 10-fold TU evaluation, four-seed LRGB evaluation, and ten-seed ESAN evaluation. The added experiments introduce no stated repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and runtime results are unchanged. New Figure 7 reports sorting accuracy of 1.0 in both multiset conditions, while adaptive ReLU achieves 1.0 without extreme elements and 0.5 with them. Appendix G.4 newly reports that both ReLU and smooth MPNNs still fail with height-3 trees and one message-passing layer.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 adds an explicit optimality statement: for n >= 4, adaptive ReLU cannot achieve an exponent below (p+1)/p. Appendix C.4 supplies a matching adversarial argument. Section 3 also changes the Wasserstein ground norm from l_p to l_1. The added proof's opening sentence reverses the inequality relative to its theorem and concluding calculation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: expected Hölder stability, depth-dependent weaknesses of sum-based MPNNs, and improved separation through sorting and adaptive ReLU. Adaptive ReLU's 3/2 exponent was already claimed in v2; the new argument supports that retained claim.

C2.justification: Remark C.6 expands v2's brief adaptive-ReLU caveat into a substantive explanation of how extreme elements widen the bias range and reduce the probability of useful separation. Appendix G.3 connects this mechanism to trained classification failures. The existing augmentation limitation and future-work discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies construction, scaling, labeling, and splitting instructions for the added multiset experiments. The code-access pointer changes from a file-hosting download to a named GitHub repository, and Table 6 corrects the SortMPNN parameter-count entry from 47.3 to 47.3K. These do not establish changes to existing implementations.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds citations to Duvenaud et al. (2015), Gama et al. (2020), Pfrommer et al. (2021), and Xu et al. (2023). It expands stability-related positioning and distinguishes Xu et al.'s fixed-topology, scalar-feature setting from the paper's graph comparison setting.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and notation edits, expands several appendix explanations, and changes the running header from a preprint notice to ICLR 2025 publication status. The overall section sequence and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel classification Figure 7 and rearranges several table and text layouts. The parameter-budget plot moves from main-text Figure 4 to appendix Figure 8; the other existing figures are retained and renumbered where necessary.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the treatment of adaptive ReLU's limits through an explicit tightness argument, a mechanism explanation, and controlled trained-model failure tests (Theorem 3.2, Remark C.6, and Figure 7). These provide useful support beyond v2's brief caveat. The gain is limited by missing uncertainty reporting for the new tests and an inequality-sign inconsistency in the added proof; the established methods and benchmark findings remain stable.
